description: I'm Metoyer! I am a sole coder, and am participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge as my first hackathon. I've only ever coded for AP Computer Science Principles and used this hackathon to learn more about numpy and scipy than make anything world-class.
summary: This program provides a time-frequency sonification of NASA's EIC data of global precipitation mapping over a sample span of five days. Accessible data is so important because everyone deserves to be a part of science, and this program bridges that gap by translating the visual information about our world that we don't think twice about into a new, resourceful program targeted towards those who need it most--low vision and blind users. Project Earth for All pushes the frontier of data processing further into comprehensibility, addresses the challenge of visualization accessibility through working with auditory perception, and works towards a world of data that can reach all.
details:
The sonification of SVS data was coded in Python. The program evaluated a sample data map of precipitation, translating longitude into time and assessing pixel values latitudinally to build the basis of the sound. Out of many different variables such as hues or brightnesses in the map, passage of time, and spatial location of the colour on the map. The creative process of choosing the variables of latitude -> frequency and pixel intensity -> amplitude (or loudness) of the audio was chosen based on the critical thinking portion of this project; how can we best suit an audio format to low vision, blind, or otherwise visually disabled users? Should the audio represent an extravagant creative masterpiece for listener's pleasure? Be as simplistic as possible to aid the user's understanding of what the variables represent--or, simply put: what actually am I hearing?

Earth for All hopes to see this technological advancement in data processing succeed for the most baseline reason that every software engineer does; we want to help people. We want to expand accessibility in STEM, and we want to see the impact of real, understandable data reaching those who may not have to opportunity to understand it in "traditional" formatting.
dataRefs: Near Real-Time Global Precipitation from the Global Precipitation Measurement Constellation
